question: What is the limiting value of compression ratio on which usually a petrol engine works?
solution:
The correct answer is __Compression ratio = 8__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Compression ratio__ is defined as the ratio of the total cylinder volume to the clearance volume in an internal combustion engine.
 
• For a petrol engine, the compression ratio typically ranges between 6:1 and 10:1.
 
• A higher compression ratio can lead to engine knocking, which is undesirable and limits the maximum value.
 
• The limiting value for a petrol engine is usually around 8 to ensure smooth operation without knocking.
 
• Petrol engines operate at lower compression ratios compared to diesel engines due to the difference in fuel ignition methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Diesel Engine Compression Ratio:**

 
 
• Diesel engines have a much higher compression ratio, typically ranging between 14:1 and 22:1.
 
• This is because diesel fuel is ignited by compression rather than a spark plug.
 
 
 
• **Knocking in Engines:**
 
 
• Engine knocking occurs when the air-fuel mixture detonates prematurely in the cylinder, causing a sharp knocking sound.
 
• High compression ratios increase the risk of knocking, especially in petrol engines.
